page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the DPLDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The system is configured with 96.0 GB of memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a bundled 1843 GB local SSD, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile characterized by strong multi-core capabilities alongside weaker single-core execution. The server achieved a strong multi-core CPU performance score of 85051.53 in stress-ng tests and a strong software compilation score of 39975.0 in Geekbench using Clang. Conversely, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1117.0 and a weak single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 8.92 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 3316.0 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 76.83 GB/sec.

This server offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from high core density and local SSD storage without requiring high memory-to-core ratios. The primary tradeoff is the lower memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core and weaker single-threaded performance. It is well-suited for parallelized tasks such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and database operations, but is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference.
